Product illustration vocabulary

The grounds and patterns every product illustration is composed from. The stack, proportions and tonal discipline come from the references; every colour and mark here is ours. Approve or cull from this sheet before the first illustration is built.

Grounds

Tonal singles for most cards. Rises when the card should stand in the colour, bleeding off the bottom. Blends for a layered pair or a mood shift — the house blend runs sky into our own teal. Deep at most once a page.

Patterns

Six, all drawn from what the product does. Each is the ground's own hue pulled 8% darker, large enough to read as texture, anchored to an edge and partly hidden behind the card. Shown here on the hue each suits best; any pattern works on any hue.

The rules that make it one system

RuleWhy
One hue per illustrationGround, pattern and every tinted control inside the card share it. A button in a second hue is the fastest way to make a card look off-system.
Pattern is tonal and behindSame hue, 8% darker, partly hidden by the card. It is texture. The moment it competes with the UI, the illustration stops reading as a product.
White card, no shadowDepth is white-on-tint. The references carry no card shadow and neither does the site.
Card is 60–80% of the frameAnd may bleed off one edge — four of nine references do. That crop is a composition move.
Nunito Sans, ladder sizes24 title · 18/16 body · 14 meta · 12 micro. 600 only on titles and button labels.
Radii: frame 28 · card 24 · controls 12–16 · pills 9999Measured from the references; one step softer than the site's own 12/16 so illustrations read as artwork, not as page cards.

Card archetypes — eight re-skinned from the references (composer, picker, settings, recap, form, assistant, chip-email, layered pair) and eight of our own (alert feed, record match, directory, rule builder, stat tile, timeline, search, toast stack) — are specified in references/illustration-system.md with the atom and molecule grammar they compose from. Any new card is one archetype, or two to four molecules, on one hue.
